name: Composition
shortDef: Assuming that what's true of the parts must be true of the whole.
definition: Concluding that a whole has a property because each of its parts has it, when the property may not carry over: small effects can add up, parts can interact, and a whole can behave differently from its pieces.
howToSpot: Is a trait of each part being stamped onto the whole?
Could the parts add up, clash or interact once they're combined?
Does the trait depend on scale, like 'small', 'safe' or 'unnoticeable'?
classicExample: Every player on our team is a star, so we'll obviously be the best team in the league.
legitimateVersion: Some traits do pass from parts to whole, like 'made entirely of steel', or 'gluten-free' when every ingredient is and nothing else gets in. It's fair when the trait truly transfers.

contrast.fal_division: Composition goes from the parts up to the whole; division goes from the whole down to its parts.
contrast.fal_hasty_generalization: Composition stamps the parts' traits onto the whole they form; hasty generalization stretches a few members' traits to all members.
